sources.cite: Kyverno documentation (release 1.13), Policy Reports: Background Scans
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: background scans validate 'existing resources in the cluster that may have been created before a policy was created', for validate and verifyImages rules; they run periodically, by default every hour; violations go to a PolicyReport or ClusterPolicyReport; background scanning is on by default and spec.background: false turns it off; results are reported whether failureAction is Audit or Enforce, and a scan 'does not block any existing resources that match a rule, even in Enforce mode'. The validate rules page (release 1.18) could not be read on 2026-11-17 (the fetch was not approved in time): the admission denial's wording and the per-rule failureAction field are from memory of Kyverno's documentation (to verify).

brief.situation: You are on the platform team at Selwyn Pay, a fictional payments company. At 13:02 a merge request switched the Kyverno ClusterPolicy require-memory-limits from Audit to Enforce. At 13:40 the payments team's hotfix for a fraud rule is refused by the cluster, and it must be live by 14:30.
handover: The policy has run in Audit with background scanning on for three weeks.
The merge request's description says 'enforce memory limits everywhere'; nobody linked the policy reports.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the policy, its reports, and the deployments it admits or refuses.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why the hotfix was refused, what you changed, and how Enforce should come back.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Connects the refusal to the switch to Enforce and what the reports already showed.
parts.modelAnswer: The validate rule's autogenerated Deployment check refused payments-api for having no memory limit. The background scan had reported it and 36 other resources in 9 namespaces for three weeks; switching to Enforce without reading those reports made every one of them fail on its next change.

parts.label: Change
parts.criteria: Brings the hotfix into compliance and stops blocking others without removing the guardrail.
parts.modelAnswer: Added a 512Mi memory limit to payments-api, sized from its 384Mi peak, so the hotfix passes the policy; set the rule back to Audit so other teams are not blocked, keeping its reports. Excluding payments or deleting the policy would have hidden the problem.

parts.label: Back to Enforce
parts.criteria: Uses the reports as the gate for enforcing.
parts.modelAnswer: Tickets list each failing resource by namespace; Enforce returns when the policy reports show zero failures, which is what the background scan is for.

guardrailRemoved.headline: One deploy, no guardrail
guardrailRemoved.body: A policy can go back to Audit in one patch and keep reporting. Deleting it, without review, removes the control for everyone to ship one change that could simply comply.

scoring.modelReasoning: The denial names the validate rule and the missing memory limit on payments-api. The policy went to Enforce 38 minutes ago, and its background scan had been reporting 37 failing resources in 9 namespaces for three weeks, so each of those will be refused on its next change. Make the hotfix comply (a 512Mi limit, sized from its 384Mi peak) rather than excluding the namespace or deleting the policy, then set the rule back to Audit so other teams are not blocked while the reports keep counting. Turning off background scans would only hide the reports. Enforce should return when the policy reports show no failures; the tickets give each owner their list.
